With the knowledge that there were friendly faces out in the wild, a Goruk exploration party was formed. At the head of the party was a minor Eye, page to the Eighth. Her name was Tsara. With her were two other pages, subservient to the Sixth. They were twins, Syril and Aglis. Each page had three Blood Tribe guards, armed with stone-tipped spears.

Bringing up the back was Daem, the son of a farmer, and only Seed Tribe member present. He had only an empty satchel, besides his food supplies. Daem's job was to find hardy plants to grow, and bring their seeds back with him.

Daem had had a hard life. In Scorch, Seed members live in the slums. Blood and Eye members constantly ignore them, only paying attention to move them out of the way, usually violently. As such, Daem had a healthy wariness of strangers and members of other Tribes.

So he was not really surprised when, about ninety days into the journey to Mount Thilla (the Shrykes had given them the location), Syril, his guards, and his twin sister's guards all turned and started killing Tsara and Aglis, as well as Tsara's guards. Naturally neither woman appreciated this, and they fought back. In the end, the Eyes three were all dead, and only four Blood members remained.

And Daem, of course, but he would not dream of being near the Blood members now. He had no map, but the mountain was visible. During the fighting, he slipped into the bushes, hiding. Soft, tall grass hid his sound. After it was all finished, he slipped away towards the nearer mountain, praying to Her that he may not be found.

Fortunately for Daem, and rather unfortunately for the four hunters, Yrt the Ninth Eye had predicted something like this and warned Eight and Six. The two had sent a second, smaller party of hunters after them, led by a page of Yrt. There were six of them, and they dispatched the traitor hunters quietly.

The burial went quickly; twelve unmarked graves were dug in a clearing. Assuming the Seed to be dead, or missing and therefore not worth the trouble, they returned to Scorch, now with each hunter's spear, and the three stone rings of the pages.

Daem was unaware of this all. Assuming the hunters to be after him and trying to kill him, Daem moved quickly and quietly to the mountain. He was not sure what he would find there; he was even less sure that it would help his situation, which grew ever more dire as his meager supply of berries drew thin.

After twenty days of methodical travel, Daem arrived at the foot of the mountain, exhausted, hungry, but no longer scared. He had established that the hunters had either lost him or given up, and they were no longer an issue. The time was right to shut his eyes and rest; Daem felt he had earned it.
